trap.label: tempo verbal
trap.wrong: Maya is waiting here since breakfast.
trap.right: Maya has been waiting here since breakfast.
trap.why: Português usa o presente com desde (“espera desde”). Inglês exige present perfect continuous.

mcq.q: When I woke up, the storm **___** raging all night.
Which means a long process up to now?

fix.wrong: The kids are playing since lunch.
fix.right: The kids have been playing since lunch.

fix.wrong: The river had flooded for days when help came.
fix.right: The river had been flooding for days when help came.

rewrite.prompt: Reescreva: “Maya waits here since breakfast.” (has been)
rewrite.answer: Maya has been waiting here since breakfast.

rewrite.prompt: Passado anterior: “We have been walking for hours.” (when it rained) (had)
rewrite.answer: We had been walking for hours when it rained.

rewrite.prompt: Reescreva: “The smoke prevents me. I breathe.” (from)
rewrite.answer: The smoke prevents me from breathing.
